open_points.subject: cross-module dependencies of the added types
open_points.text: the types that cross module boundaries without a meaning of their own in State 1
open_points.question: Which consumer modules directly import each of `SourceRead`, `ScanResult`, `MarkOutcome`, `DeliverRequest`, `PublishedRequest` and `HealthAnswer` from `domain_models`?
options: Declare a separate minimal consumer-to-`domain_models` edge for every directly used type
Have `deliverer_api` own all route DTO dependencies while operation modules import only their result types
Let operation modules also import the request and response DTOs
open_points.default_guess: Declare minimal per-symbol edges: operation modules import only their inputs and results, and `deliverer_api` imports the route DTOs plus operation results it names.

open_points.subject: SourceRead
open_points.text: `SourceRead`, a `SourceFile` with the bytes that were judged
open_points.question: What is the exact field structure of `SourceRead`, including the field name and type of the bytes and whether `SourceFile` is nested, inherited or flattened?
options: `SourceRead(source: SourceFile, data: bytes)`
A flattened value containing every `SourceFile` field plus `data: bytes`
A subtype of `SourceFile` that adds a bytes field

open_points.subject: SourceRead bytes
open_points.question: Which bytes must this field preserve, and may a consumer reread the server path instead of using them?
options: The exact source bytes on which the file judgment was made, which all subsequent work must use
The prepared or normalized image bytes produced after judgment
An optional snapshot that consumers may replace by rereading the path
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the exact judged source bytes and require consumers to use that snapshot.

open_points.subject: ScanResult
open_points.text: `ScanResult`, the observations of one scan and the count of each status
open_points.question: What are the exact fields and types of `ScanResult`, including the observation collection, its ordering and the representation of status counts?
options: An ordered sequence of M02 observations plus `dict[ScanStatus, int]` containing every status
An ordered sequence plus one integer field per status
Only the observations, with counts exposed as derived properties
open_points.default_guess: Use an ordered sequence of observations and a mapping containing every `ScanStatus`, including zero counts.

open_points.subject: ScanResult status counts
open_points.text: the observations of one scan and the count of each status
open_points.question: Must each status count equal the number of observations with that status, and is that equality enforced by construction or merely expected of the producer?
options: Derive counts from observations so disagreement is impossible
Store counts and validate equality when constructing `ScanResult`
Store both without enforcing equality
open_points.default_guess: Derive the counts from the observations.

open_points.subject: MarkOutcome
open_points.question: What is the exact structure of `MarkOutcome`, and does it contain a `PublicationMark` value plus a non-persisted `MarkStatus`, flatten M07's fields, or alter M07 itself?
options: `MarkOutcome(mark: PublicationMark, status: MarkStatus)`
A flattened result containing all M07 fields and `status`
Add `status` to M07 even though State 1 says it is not stored
open_points.default_guess: Use a wrapper containing `mark: PublicationMark` and `status: MarkStatus`, leaving M07 unchanged.

open_points.subject: DeliverRequest
open_points.text: `DeliverRequest` and `PublishedRequest`, the bodies of two routes
open_points.question: Which route consumes `DeliverRequest`, and what are all of its fields, types, required values and defaults?
options: A deliver-one-photo body containing project and source identity
A body containing project identity and a complete `SourceRead`
A body containing project identity, source identity and caller-selected publication metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use a deliver-one-photo request containing `project_id` and `source_id`, with no server path or bytes supplied by the caller.

open_points.subject: PublishedRequest
open_points.text: `DeliverRequest` and `PublishedRequest`, the bodies of two routes
open_points.question: Which route consumes `PublishedRequest`, and what are all of its fields, types, required values and defaults?
options: A publication-mark request containing `project_id`, `source_id` and Portal `photo_id`
A request containing a placement reference and Portal `photo_id`
The complete M05 publication body returned by the Portal caller
open_points.default_guess: Use a publication-mark request containing `project_id`, `source_id` and `photo_id`.

open_points.subject: DeliverRequest and PublishedRequest route mapping
open_points.question: What are the two routes, and which request type belongs to each one?
options: `DeliverRequest` belongs to the deliver operation and `PublishedRequest` to the record-publication operation
Both are alternative bodies of one delivery route
The names refer to transport routes whose operation mapping is defined elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Map `DeliverRequest` to delivery and `PublishedRequest` to recording publication.

open_points.subject: HealthAnswer
open_points.text: `HealthAnswer`, the body of the health route
open_points.question: What is the exact field structure and closed set of values of `HealthAnswer`?
options: A single boolean health field
A status string with a closed value such as `ok`
A structured answer containing separate state, binary-store and connections checks
open_points.default_guess: Use a single closed status value representing that the service process is healthy.
